reportSubtitle: Cost per inquiry nearly halved, and the new Google page is live
summary:
Two weeks ago I set up a focused test: point the budget at bartender-hire searches, launch a landing page built specifically for people coming from Google, and give it a clean run. This report is the read on that test.

The headline is that cost per inquiry nearly halved, from about $560 to $314, and it is still moving in the right direction. We brought in three inquiries this period. The most encouraging one came in at $5.72, from someone searching a bartender term with the city in it, which is the single cheapest inquiry this account has ever produced. That is exactly the kind of search we rebuilt the account around.

The one thing still holding the average up is a single broad 'party' keyword that spends a lot for very little. I have been trimming its budget and steering money toward the exact bartender terms that convert cheaply. As that shift continues, the blended cost per inquiry should keep falling toward the account's historical best. Detail below.

findings.title: Cost per inquiry nearly halved, and the cheapest came from a city search
findings.description: Blended cost per inquiry dropped from $560 to $314 in a single cycle, and inquiries rose from two to three. The standout is a booking inquiry that came in at $5.72 from a search that paired the service with the city ('bartenders denver'). That is the cheapest inquiry the account has ever produced, and it confirms that city plus bartender is the highest-value search we can win.

findings.title: The exact bartender terms convert far cheaper than the broad ones
findings.description: Both of this period's efficient inquiries came through exact-match terms: 'bartenders denver' at $5.72 and 'bartenders for hire' at $110.76. The one expensive inquiry, at $473, came through a broad 'party' phrase that pulls a wide, mixed set of searches. The lesson is consistent with the account's whole history: the tighter and more specific the term, the cheaper the inquiry.

findings.title: One 'party' keyword still carries most of the cost
findings.description: A single phrase keyword, 'bartender for party', took the largest share of the budget this period for just one inquiry. Because it matches loosely across many 'party' searches, it draws clicks that rarely book. It is the clearest remaining source of inefficiency, and steering its budget toward the proven exact terms is what will keep the average falling.

actions.title: Paused the broad keyword pulling low-intent traffic
actions.description: Turned off the broad 'party' term that was drawing browse-only searches, so the budget flows to searches with real hire intent.

actions.title: Concentrated the budget on the proven bartender terms
actions.description: Lowered bids on the expensive and lowest-quality terms and protected the exact bartender and city terms that are converting cheaply, so more of each day's budget reaches the searches that book.

actions.title: Tuned the landing page for faster mobile load
actions.description: Improved how quickly the page loads on phones and tightened up its accessibility, so more of the people who click actually stay and reach the form.

nextSteps: Keep concentrating the budget on the exact bartender and city terms and watch cost per inquiry continue to fall.
